Indikator 5 tracks the incidence of ischemic stroke among prevalent patients with atrial fibrillation, measuring healthcare quality against a national standard of ≤ 0.8%. The data compiled from the 2023, 2024, and 2025 reports spans multiple geographic and organizational levels—including national, regional, municipal, and health cluster divisions—offering a comprehensive view of stroke prevention efficacy over time.

At the national level, Denmark consistently meets the quality standard, maintaining an incidence of 0.8% across the 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24, and 2024/25 periods [^src1], [^src3], [^src5]. Regionally, a distinct geographic divide emerges. [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] generally meet the target. Midtjylland demonstrates notable improvement, successfully lowering its incidence to 0.6% in the 2024/25 period [^src5]. In contrast, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] consistently fail to meet the standard. Hovedstaden recorded a 1.0% incidence in both the 2023/24 and 2024/25 periods [^src3], [^src5], while Sjælland remained at 0.9% or 1.0% across the tracked years [^src1], [^src5].

At the municipal level (based on 2022/23 data), the majority of municipalities met the standard. Leaders such as [[toender|Tønder]], [[skive|Skive]], and [[frederikshavn|Frederikshavn]] achieved low incidences of 0.4% [^src2]. However, outliers like [[samsoe|Samsø]], [[norddjurs|Norddjurs]], and [[morsoe|Morsø]] exceeded the target with 1.5% incidences [^src2]. These high values are heavily influenced by small population denominators, resulting in wide confidence intervals; for instance, Samsø's 1.5% incidence carried a 95% CI of 0.2-5.4 [^src2]. Small island municipalities like [[laesoe|Læsø]] and [[aeroe|Ærø]] similarly act as statistical outliers, exhibiting high variance that complicates direct comparison with larger mainland municipalities [^src2].

Among health clusters, performance is equally mixed. [[sundhedsklynge-soenderjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland]] and [[goedstrupklyngen|Gødstrupklyngen]] performed exceptionally well, both reaching 0.5% in the 2024/25 period [^src5]. Conversely, clusters such as [[sundhedsklynge-midt|Sundhedsklynge Midt]] and [[sundhedsklynge-byen|Sundhedsklynge Byen]] struggled to meet the threshold. Sundhedsklynge Midt recorded a 1.1% incidence in 2022/23 and remained above the 0.8% standard in subsequent years [^src3], [^src5]. Meanwhile, [[klynge-vest|Klynge VEST]] demonstrated significant fluctuation, missing the standard with 1.2% in 2022/23 before improving to 0.7% in 2023/24 [^src4], [^src5]. 

Ultimately, the data reveals a persistent structural challenge in eastern Denmark, where Hovedstaden and Sjælland continue to lag behind their western and northern counterparts in preventing ischemic strokes among atrial fibrillation patients.
